text: The evidence is silent on contrition as something extended from one person to another. Contrition is a condition of the inner being before God, not a characteristic extended toward other humans. The absence of a giving direction is structurally consistent with contrition's nature: it is intrinsically the posture of the self before God, not a relational commodity extended outward. This silence is complete and informative — it distinguishes contrition from characteristics like forgiveness, mercy, and compassion that have a constitutive giving direction.

The verse evidence is largely silent on the horizontal giving direction of contrition. The characteristic operates primarily in the vertical (human before God). The substitutionary group is the nearest approximation but is unique to the Servant. The horizontal relational dimension is a consistent thin-evidence gap in this registry. OBS-030-041.

**[CHAR-2]** E — VCG-01 involves humans extending CHAR-2 to other humans: Ammonites shaving David's envoys, tenants beating servants. In the unjust register, CHAR-2 is inflicted by malicious agents. In the corrective register, legitimate authority can impose CHAR-2 as a judicial act. The giving direction is morally ambiguous — it can be unjust infliction or just correction.

**[CHAR-3]** E — VCG-01 is primarily about humans extending dishonour toward other humans or toward God. The unjust judge (Luk 18:2/4) extends worth-denial to the widow. The rich receive honor while the poor man is dishonored (Jam 2:6). The head-covering symbolic acts extend disrespect toward divinely ordered authority structures.

---

**[CHAR-4]** E — CHAR-4 can be extended interpersonally through the articulation of moral evaluations: Paul's renunciation of shameful ways (2Cor 4:2) is both his own functioning CHAR-4 and an implicit invitation to the community's conscience to recognise the same standard. 1Cor 14:35's articulated moral-evaluative judgment extends a community's shared CHAR-4 evaluation.

---

**[CHAR-5]** E — The contempt-er extends CHAR-5 toward others through VCG-01's dismissive attitude, VCG-02's violent rejection, and VCG-03's verbal contempt. In every mode, the extending person must have a prior inner disposition of self-elevation or self-righteousness (Luk 18:9) to sustain the contemptuous dismissal of others. The person who gives CHAR-5 is one who has placed themselves above the person they despise — they must have an inflated inner self-assessment as the precondition for the contempt-extension.

**[CHAR-6]** S — The 8-verse corpus does not evidence CHAR-6 being extended by one person toward another in a direct relational-giving sense. CHAR-6 is an inner moral condition of the individual, not primarily a characteristic extended toward others. Silent on the giving direction as a direct relational-extension.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The human giving of M07's characteristics spans a moral spectrum from unjust to legitimate. At the unjust pole: humans inflicting shame through military conquest (Char 2), extending worth-denial through favoritism and hypocrisy (Char 3), and directing contemptuous dismissal toward others (Char 5). At the legitimate-corrective pole: humans deploying corrective shame for moral formation (Char 1's entrepō passages — 2Th 3:14; 1Cor 6:5; Char 4's articulated moral evaluation). Cluster-level finding: the same characteristics that name the unjust forms also name their legitimate forms. The moral quality of the giving depends on whether the giver is aligned with God's own movement in the shame-field — God abases the proud justly; humans can enact the same correction legitimately (corrective community discipline) or unjustly (violence, contempt, worth-denial). The inner conditions enabling legitimate extension: genuine moral concern for the shamed person, not desire for their destruction; a grounded own moral position; recognition of the person's worth even in correction.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The characteristic operates in transmission (involuntary) rather than giving (intentional). The evidence documents the transmission mechanism extensively; the "giving" frame is not applicable to the ritual defilement-state.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The giving/transmitting direction is evidenced in the environmental-formative mode (1Cor 8:7 formative association; 2Cor 6:17 community immersion). Not fully silent, but the evidence is indirect rather than direct transmission.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The extending/transmitting direction is evidenced (Gen 34, Eze 23:17, Lam 4:15). Not fully silent, though the "giving" frame requires reframing as "extending through violation or contagion" in this characteristic's register.

**[CHAR-4]** S — The evidence is silent on person-to-person extension of the characteristic. The characteristic is imposed by spiritual agents, not transmitted through human-to-human interaction. This is a structural feature distinguishing Characteristic 4 from all other M10c characteristics: it has no human-giving dimension.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Characteristic 4 is silent on human-person-to-human-person extension. Characteristics 1, 2, and 3 all evidence person-to-person extension or transmission in different modes. The 3:1 silence pattern is analytically significant and confirms Characteristic 4's structural distinctiveness as the only M10c characteristic with no human-transmission mechanism.
